C9000283.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 283 (Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle.; papers: Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_MAIN_SYNTHESIS.statement: For n>=1 a uniform polynomial-time fixed-gate Boolean-oracle circuit approximates every n-qubit unitary channel within full diamond norm 1/2 after choosing the oracle; no efficient oracle construction is asserted (thm:main).

C_RECURSION.statement: A single smaller-circuit call per recursion level yields the uniform clean programmable synthesis bound (rec:step and rec:skeleton).

C_CONTRACTION.statement: Uniform conditioning produces an internal contraction of norm at most 3/4 with the stated dimension decrease and slot resources (contract:moment, contract:block, contract:depth).

C_CLEAN_ENCODING.statement: Row-sparse near-isometries have the claimed coherent clean encoders and resource bounds (encode:row-sparse and encode:implementation).

C_COMPILATION.statement: Phase-sensitive uniformly controlled slots compile into H,T,T-dagger,CNOT and one Boolean oracle with the claimed polynomial resources (compile:words and compile:slots).

C_SLOT_INTERFACE.statement: The state preparation, permutation and positive-phase Fourier slot skeletons satisfy their uniform clean interfaces (slot:preparation, slot:permutation, slot:fourier).

C_FOURIER_FIELDS.statement: Under every hypothesis of Section 04, feedback is unitary with FE*=R*V, both field Grams lie between (1-r^(2L))I and I, both positive-phase Fourier matrices have row support at most L, and truncated intertwining error is at most 2r^L/(1-r).

C_FOURIER_CORE.statement: Universal formal core: block feedback unitarity and exact intertwining given the solved stable feedback equation; both ordered Gram defect identities and orthogonal coefficient expansion; characteristic-safe Newton reconstruction; the actual binary moment code; and both signed full-row bounds, with a compact prime-field extension. Analytic bridges are separate prose obligations.

C_FEEDBACK.statement: For every admissible complex unitary block matrix and diagonal unitary feedback, the stable resolvent defines a unitary F and the exact forward/backward intertwining and Y formulas (fields:unitary).

C_FIELD_GRAMS.statement: Positive and negative common-phase degrees are distinct modulo 2^b; both averaged field Grams have the claimed Loewner bounds, with the backward product ordered as Z*D*.

C_FIELD_SUPPORT.statement: With the positive-phase Fourier convention, E has negative multiset frequencies and R has positive ones; nonzero rows are supported only on members of one length-at-most-L multiset, and the zero row on one port.

C_FIELD_ERROR.statement: Stable Neumann tails and the pointwise exact identity imply the field operator-norm error at most 2r^L/(1-r), including r=0 and L=1.

C_COMPACT_GRID.statement: For every prime p>max(s,L), the grid (Z/p)^(L+1) with the same moment-curve phases has all the Section 04 feedback, Gram, signed row-support and error conclusions. One may choose max(s,L)<p<=2max(s,L), reducing the logarithmic grid size to at most (L+1)log2(2max(s,L)); no binary-slot implementation bound is inferred.

C_TRANSFER_CONTEXT.statement: The classical scalar-variable characteristic function of a finite-dimensional unitary colligation is rational inner; this contextual citation is not a dependency of the diagonal-feedback proof.
